metadata.title: Matt Pocock 实战教程：用一个技能拯救被AI写烂的代码库 —— improve-codebase-architecture【中英字幕】
metadata.description:
Matt Pocock 用他的 improve codebase architecture 技能，演示如何把一个被 AI 加速腐化的代码库救回来——核心是 John Ousterhout《A Philosophy of Software Design》里的"深模块"思想。

为什么值得看：
1. AI 为什么让代码库烂得更快：软件熵、以及那个越滚越大的"泥球"是怎么来的
2. 一套和 AI 对话的共享术语：模块 / 接口 / 接缝 / 适配器 / 局部性 / 杠杆，让你提需求更精准
3. 完整实操：在真实项目里跑技能 → 选出深化候选 → grilling 环节 → 落地成 issue 交给 AFK agent

关键内容：
· 软件熵：每一次不顾全局的改动，都在给代码库埋下难维护的隐患
· 深模块 vs 浅模块：用一个小接口，藏住一大片实现
· 深度 / 局部性 / 杠杆：衡量一个模块好不好用的三个维度
· 接缝与适配器：在哪里做测试、怎么在不改业务的前提下替换实现
· 技能工作流：探索代码 → HTML 候选报告 → grilling 逐条拷问 → to-prd / to-issues 落地
· 人机分工：agent 是冲锋的战术"士官"，你才是拍板的战略"将军"

来源：
· 原视频：https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3MP8D-mdheA

字幕：AI 辅助转录 + 翻译并经人工校对。如有不准确之处，欢迎指出。

claims.claim: The speaker says his GitHub skills repository had about 41.5 thousand stars at recording time.
claims.video_statement: The speaker says his GitHub skills repository had about 41.5 thousand stars at recording time.
claims.verified_result: Unverified as a historical point-in-time count. The official repository exists and its live GitHub page exposes the current star count, but that changing value does not establish the count on the unknown recording date. No authoritative archived snapshot tied to the recording was available in this check.

claims.claim: The deep-module and shallow-module concepts are attributed to John Ousterhout’s book A Philosophy of Software Design.
claims.video_statement: The deep-module and shallow-module concepts are attributed to John Ousterhout’s book A Philosophy of Software Design.
claims.verified_result: Partially confirmed. John Ousterhout's official Stanford page confirms that *A Philosophy of Software Design* is his book, and Matt Pocock's official codebase-design material uses the deep-versus-shallow module vocabulary. However, the sources reviewed here do not directly locate a passage in Ousterhout's book establishing that provenance, so the video's attribution remains plausible but was not independently confirmed from the book text.

sources.title: John Ousterhout — A Philosophy of Software Design

claims.claim: The video calls the locations where modules interface with one another seams.
claims.video_statement: The video calls the locations where modules interface with one another seams.
claims.verified_result: Partially confirmed as the video's adopted design vocabulary, not as a universal definition. Matt Pocock's official glossary defines a seam as the location at which a module's interface lives and attributes the underlying term to Michael Feathers. Feathers' own published definition is broader: a place where behavior can be altered without editing that place.

sources.title: Michael Feathers — Seams (Working Effectively with Legacy Code excerpt)

claims.claim: The video uses adapter for a concrete module satisfying the interface at a seam, drawing the term from hexagonal architecture.
claims.video_statement: The video uses adapter for a concrete module satisfying the interface at a seam, drawing the term from hexagonal architecture.
claims.verified_result: Confirmed with a terminology caveat. Matt Pocock's official glossary defines an adapter as a concrete thing satisfying an interface at a seam. Alistair Cockburn's original Hexagonal Architecture article is explicitly titled Ports and Adapters and describes technology-specific adapters converting between a port's protocol and external devices. Cockburn also notes that the generic Adapter pattern predates his ports-and-adapters pattern, so the word itself did not originate with hexagonal architecture.

sources.title: Alistair Cockburn — Hexagonal Architecture: the original 2005 article
